versions.research_rationale:
EO 6242D (August 04, 1933, Franklin D. Roosevelt) is read in full in the held American Presidency Project transcription (jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-6242-d-the-matter-the-application-crystal-springs-bleachery-incorporated.txt; grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; APP node 362065; common-crawl capture 2025-11-09T04:25:59Z). APP page check under AGENT_PROTOCOL.md: the MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl row with the same sha256 (8d83f0a0afb2...) has heading 'Executive Order 6242-D—In the Matter of the Application of Crystal Springs Bleachery Incorporated for Certain Stay of Application and Exemptions from the Cotton Textile Code' and date 1933-08-04, the heading's number and subject and the date agree with the text (which ends 'The White House, ...' with the same date), and the row's text_sha256 equals the held file's text_sha256 (b1d83322a27f...). The text is complete (operative paragraph, signature, recommendation line and date). Identity: the census register (jobs/domesday-register/output/REGISTER.csv) title 'Executive Order 6242-D—In the Matter of the Application of Crystal Springs Bleachery Incorporated for Certain Stay of Application and Exemptions from the Cotton Textile Code' dated 1933-08-04 and the WPA 1944 numbered-list summary 'Application of the Crystal Springs Bleachery for ex emptions from the Code of Fair Competition for the Cotton Textile In dustry denied. I NRA Codes 726.' agree with the text. original not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved. Operative command: the order denies the application of the named applicants (Crystal Springs Bleachery Incorporated, per the title) for an exemption from the Cotton Textile Industry code as to productive machinery: 'do order that the application for exemption by the above-named applicants be, and it is hereby denied, except as said applicants may be affected by the stay of the code granted by the Administrator's order of July 30, 1933, pending my final determination of the issues raised in the application for exemption filed by the Rubber Manufacturer's Association with reference to the limitation of use of machinery for the production of tire yarns or fabrics for rubber tires.' Clause inventory: the machine inventory is accepted as complete (one clause, the operative paragraph with its signature and recommendation lines). The order is a determination under section 3 of the Act and the July 15, 1933 hearing procedure. It commands no person to act; its only legal consequence is that the applicants stay bound by the code's provisions, a consequence that exists only while the code is enforceable. The alternative reading, that a denial is exhausted on signing, is not adopted because the denial's operative content (refusing an exemption from a code that continued to bind) lasted as long as the code's enforceability did. First end: 1935-06-14, by S.J. Res. 113 section 2 (SUPPLEMENT:SJRES113), the first end of a code-dependent clause with no earlier own-terms end and no earlier cancellation, supersession or suspension held. Schechter (May 27, 1935) is recorded as a validity characterization and not as the end date.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The words 'pending my final determination' describe the duration of the Administrator's July 30, 1933 stay, which is the Administrator's instrument and not this order's command; this order does not grant, extend or define the stay. The dossier's own-terms records for this order are machine 'report_deadline' leads on the July 15, 1933 report, which is a recital, and a report deadline is never an end. The held orders on the machine-hour stay are later events, not ends of the denial: EO 6407 (November 6, 1933), EO 6424 (November 13, 1933) and EO 6463 (November 27, 1933) set and extended the termination of the Administrator's stay, and EO 6476 (December 4, 1933) denied the Rubber Manufacturers' application, terminated the stay, and made the code's machine-hour limitation 'in full force and effect from and after December 11, 1933'. EO 6420-A (November 9, 1933) and later cotton-textile orders modify or administer the code and do not cancel it. Searches on 2026-10-29 of held evidence: the held order texts (jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts: every order numbered 6180 through 7076 that mentions codes of fair competition, NRA or the National Industrial Recovery Act was scanned for the words cancel, revoke, rescind, supersede, terminate, annul and void; every held text folder except the Federal Register and source-ladder folders was searched for citations of this order's number and for the code's name); the census-register titles (jobs/domesday-register/output/REGISTER.csv); and the 1933-1935 summaries of the WPA 1944 numbered list (jobs/x1-class-engine/data/WPA_NUMBERED_ENTRIES.csv). The only held cancellation of a code approval in the period is EO 6925-A (December 19, 1934), which cancels the approval of the Cinders, Ashes and Scavenger Trade code after a hearing, under Article VIII of that code and Title I. No held record cancels, revokes, suspends or supersedes this code before June 14, 1935. General orders that touch approved codes are not ends of this clause: EO 6354 (October 23, 1933) as amended by EO 6710 (May 15, 1934) excepts small local retail and service employers in towns under 2,500 population from code provisions on hours, pay, minimum prices and assessments; EO 6723 (May 26, 1934) suspends code provisions other than child labor, maximum hours, minimum pay and sections 7(a) and 10(b) for service trades the Administrator later designates. Each reaches only a class of persons or of designated trades and leaves the approval operative for everyone else; no held record designates this code's trade under EO 6723. June 16, 1935 is not an end: section 1 of S.J. Res. 113 replaced the section 2(c) two-year expiry with April 1, 1936 (SUPPLEMENT:NIRA2C, SUPPLEMENT:SJRES113). EO 7075 (June 15, 1935) and EO 7252 (December 21, 1935) concern NRA administration. EO 7076 (June 15, 1935) continues existing Title I orders 'so far as consistent with' Title I as amended and says it is not an exercise of authority 'to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition, to provide for the enforcement of such codes'; it does not restore the enforcement that section 2 repealed, so it does not continue this approval. The approval therefore has no earlier end than the statutory repeal.","independent_command_check":"The order's only operative command is stated above; it contains no appointment, delegation, direction to an agency or other command that is independent of the code approval, and nothing in it rests on a statute other than Title I. The report of July 15, 1933 adopted in the recital and the recommendation by Hugh S. Johnson are not commands.","savings_check":"Acts done and liabilities incurred under the code before June 14, 1935 (violations, injunctions, convictions, compliance) are completed or accrued effects and are not continued operation of the approval. The section 5 antitrust exemption for a code approved and in effect and for action complying with it during the period (SUPPLEMENT:NIRA5) is accrued to the extent it covers action already taken; the resolution's proviso says the exemption 'shall extend only to agreements and action thereunder' putting section 7(a) requirements into effect or prohibiting practices already unlawful, names agreements rather than codes and states no time limit, and the held text does not settle whether it narrowed the exemption for action taken under codes before June 14, 1935. No held source continues this approval after June 14, 1935, and later statutes that regulated an industry are independent laws.","scope_check":"Single clause; the repeal reaches the whole of it: every effect of the order ran through section 3 of the Act, which section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 repealed by description (power to approve or prescribe codes and the provisions for enforcing them). The sole operative command is the denial. Its exception recognizes the Administrator's stay as a limit on the denial's reach for as long as that stay lasted; EO 6476 ended the stay with effect from December 11, 1933, after which the exception had nothing to reach and the denial applied without it. That narrowing of the exception is a later event; the denial itself continued as to the applicants."}

savings_residuals.reason: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the code before June 14, 1935 (violations, injunctions, convictions, compliance) are completed or accrued effects and are not continued operation of the approval. The section 5 antitrust exemption for a code approved and in effect and for action complying with it during the period (SUPPLEMENT:NIRA5) is accrued to the extent it covers action already taken; the resolution's proviso says the exemption 'shall extend only to agreements and action thereunder' putting section 7(a) requirements into effect or prohibiting practices already unlawful, names agreements rather than codes and states no time limit, and the held text does not settle whether it narrowed the exemption for action taken under codes before June 14, 1935. No held source continues this approval after June 14, 1935, and later statutes that regulated an industry are independent laws.
